bet.text: Throughput: a wide drum shooter fed by a ball path as wide as possible with no interruptions, in place of a turret.

demand.text: Shoot and hold more fuel: the first robot's turret shot about eight balls a second, the drum about 23, and capacity went from about 35 to about 60 to 70.

auto.text: The stowed four-bar intake does not fit under the trench, which the team calls worse for autonomous.
Before the championship, a 5687 mentor recalled its auto as the best of the New England contenders, after 2056.

cycle.text: Fuel goes from the intake over a roller floor, through a double roller, to the drum.
One button locks onto the target or onto passing.
A partner team describes aggressive fuel poaching; a poster reports a 908 point alliance score in qualifications, called a record.

fallback.text: If pose is lost, the operator presses a button that aligns without it.

gave_up.text: The intake cannot pass the trench stowed.
Cast intake wheels lasted about one event plus practice.
In the New England final a defender held it at the bump; its drive coach calls it a pin that cost a cycle.
Another poster says it was beached on fuel.

changed.text: Roman I had a turret and spindexer.
It won its first event in March, a newspaper reports.
Seeing 5687's robot and its advice set Roman II in motion.
CAD took about four days, building about a week and a half, with about a week left to drive and code.
The new intake is more compact, after a long bar kept bending, and a third Limelight went on the shooter.

outcome.text: 61-15-1 in official play; won the Hopper division; pick 1 of the Hopper alliance on Einstein; ranked 25 by championship OPR (273.27, Hopper).

cost.text: It does not fit under the trench while stowed, which was worse for autonomous
Wheels lasted about one event plus hours of practice; the team says stock wheels were probably the better choice for durability

facts.text: Geometry is made to fold during impacts, and the team says it worked
Arms are stacked plates of SRPP and polycarbonate with 3/8 in spacers through the pivot, driven by SplineXL
Wheels are cast by the team in VytaFlex 30
Short stub shafts on 3/8 hex replace full-length roller shafts to save weight

solves.text: Hold more fuel than the first robot

cost.text: In a New England Championship division final the net caught in the shooter hood rollers, and with a minute and a half left it could not shoot

facts.text: The net adds about
Total capacity about 60 to 70 balls, against about 35 with the old intake

solves.text: Move a full load without jamming or sagging

facts.text: The path is as wide as possible with no interruptions, which made jamming virtually impossible
3:1 reduction to the front roller, about 2:1 to the rest, on one motor
Rollers (which ones is not said) have spread-out flex wheels for an uneven surface and less taping, with grip tape
It pivots on the intake's SplineXL as a dead shaft, giving access to the electronics
It pushes balls down and around a UHMW lower hood with very low compression
The feed plate is laser-cut UHMW sheet bolted into shape
Feed speed was raised until it hurt the shot

solves.text: Shoot far more balls a second than the turret did

facts.text: Rate claimed, about
Aluminum tube with custom prints around it, covered in cat tongue tape
No lathe was big enough, so radial holes were drilled with printed guides
No drive parts outside it except the hood's sector gear; axles are dead
The adjustable hood runs on brass bushings

solves.text: Aim and pass with one button

facts.text: Limelights track AprilTags; a third one is on the shooter
Shooter speed and hood rise with distance
The hood drops by itself near the trench, in a zone that grows with speed

decisions.because: the turret shot about eight balls a second and the drum about 23
it folds out of the way in heavy impacts, and the team had more experience with it
decisions.cost: it did not fit under the trench while stowed, worse for autonomous

decisions.because: a belted floor might sag under the weight of all the balls
decisions.cost: it took experiments with traction to get the flow right

decisions.because: the chosen ratio ran smoothly without an aggressive current limit, so another motor gave little benefit

decisions.choice: Flex wheels and grip tape on rollers
decisions.because: WCP silicone was out of stock and equivalent tube was expensive
the old wheels walked on the dead-axle tubes and there were not enough for two robots
decisions.cost: about one event plus practice of life
